title: Wallpaper cache
line: Images you pick as your wallpaper are now kept in Plasma's wallpaper folder, so deleting or moving the original file no longer resets the desktop to the default.
explanation: The Image wallpaper stores the path of the file the user picked, so once that file is deleted, moved or on an unmounted disk, the next login falls back to the default wallpaper. When a single image from outside the wallpaper folders is applied in the wallpaper settings, it is now copied into ~/.local/share/wallpapers/ and the setting points at the copy; the gallery entry for the original is replaced by the copy, which can still be removed with its X button. Installed wallpapers and packages are left alone, a copy with the same name and content is reused, and a different file with the same name gets a "name (1).png" copy.

commits.message:
wallpapers/image: keep a copy of the user's chosen wallpaper image

The wallpaper pointed at the file the user picked, so deleting, moving or
unmounting it reset the desktop to the default. When an image from outside
the wallpaper folders is applied, copy it into the local wallpapers folder.

BUG: 399905

media.caption: With the fix: myphoto.png picked in the wallpaper settings and applied (the setting now points at ~/.local/share/wallpapers/myphoto.png)
Master: after deleting ~/Downloads/myphoto.png and restarting plasmashell, the desktop is back to the default wallpaper
With the fix: same steps, the chosen picture stays
Master: the gallery entry is the file in ~/Downloads
With the fix: the gallery shows the kept copies, one entry each; a second, different myphoto.png from ~/Pictures became "myphoto (1)"
